topic: Polyglot Kubernetes AI Stack Overview & Compute Optimization
content: Brighton Kimani engineered a low-footprint polyglot AI microservice architecture in the ai-stack Kubernetes namespace (https://github.com/Gachagokimani/kubernetes-llm-hosting-stack) designed to run under 4 GB RAM. It decouples five specialized services: llama-server (C++ llama.cpp running Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct Q4_K_M GGUF on CPU, NodePort 30880), SearXNG (privacy-first meta-search engine, NodePort 30881), rag-frontend (FastAPI Python RAG orchestrator and portfolio UI, NodePort 30882), pdf-ingest-dotnet (.NET 8 Minimal API gateway for PDF ingestion, Markdown stripping, and dual PVC + PostgreSQL persistence), and doc-indexer-spring (Java HTTP indexer syncing offer/proposal PDFs into /shared/kb/proposals_offers.json).

topic: .NET 8 OAuth 2.0 SSO RBAC Microservice & Policy Decision Point
content: Brighton built a standalone .NET 8 RBAC and OAuth 2.0 SSO microservice (services/dotnet-rbac) deployable independently via k8s-deployment.yaml. It authenticates GitHub OAuth users against ADMIN_ALLOWED_IDS, mints HttpOnly HMAC-SHA256 JWT cookies (bk_sso_token), exposes a Policy Decision Point (/api/rbac/authorize), and strictly gates the Proposals navbar link, PDF upload bar, and private Proposals Vault so only Brighton Kimani has escalated admin access while public visitors remain read-only guests.

topic: Kubernetes Secrets, ConfigMaps & etcd Encryption Hardening
content: In manifests/security/configmap-and-secret.yaml, Brighton centralized non-sensitive service endpoints into ai-stack-config (ConfigMap) and isolated OAuth client secrets, JWT signing keys, and PostgreSQL connection strings into ai-stack-secrets (Opaque Secret) backed by kube-apiserver EncryptionConfiguration (aescbc) for etcd encryption at rest.
